source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A food vendor harbors Salmonella typhi and can spread it but has no symptoms. What is she?
questions.rationale: A carrier harbors the organism and can transmit it to a susceptible host without showing signs of the disease. A contact is someone in close association with an infected person.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Communicable Disease Terminologies (PDF p. 142)
questions.quote: An individual who harbors the organism and is capable of transmitting it to a susceptible host without showing manifestations of the disease.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: The nurse disinfects a patient's sputum cup right after he coughs into it while he is still infectious. This is:
questions.rationale: Concurrent disinfection is done immediately after the infected person discharges infectious material, while the patient is still the source of infection. Terminal disinfection is done after discharge.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Communicable Disease Terminologies (PDF p. 142)
questions.quote: Method of disinfection when the patient is still the source of infection.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Exposed persons have their movement limited for the longest incubation period of the disease. This is:
questions.rationale: Quarantine limits the movement of exposed persons or animals for the longest incubation period. Isolation separates infected persons during the period of communicability.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Communicable Disease Terminologies (PDF p. 142)
questions.quote: for a period of time equivalent to the longest incubation period of that disease.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Schistosomiasis is always present at a fairly constant level in Leyte and Samar. This pattern is:
questions.rationale: Endemic means continuous occurrence of the usual number of cases in a locality, such as schistosomiasis in Leyte and Samar, filariasis in Sorsogon, and malaria in Palawan.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Patterns of Occurrence (PDF p. 143)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A town has a few isolated, unrelated rabies cases this year. Which pattern is this?
questions.rationale: Sporadic occurrence is the intermittent appearance of a few isolated, unrelated cases in a locality, such as rabies.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Patterns of Occurrence (PDF p. 143)
questions.quote: Intermittent occurrence of a few isolated and unrelated cases in a given locality.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which link in the chain of infection is the EASIEST to break?
questions.rationale: The mode of transmission is the easiest link to break, for example through handwashing and barriers. Contact is the most common mode.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Chain of Infection (PDF p. 143)
questions.quote: Easiest link to break the chain of infection

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Droplet transmission is generally limited to what distance?
questions.rationale: Droplet spread from coughing, sneezing, or talking is limited to about 3 feet. Airborne particles stay suspended and travel farther.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mode of Transmission (PDF p. 144)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A newborn has antibodies received through the placenta. Which type of immunity is this?
questions.rationale: Natural passive immunity is acquired through placental transfer. Natural active comes from recovering from disease.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A dog-bite victim receives rabies immunoglobulin. Which type of immunity does this give?
questions.rationale: Artificial passive immunity comes from antitoxin, antiserum, convalescent serum, or immunoglobulins. Vaccines and toxoids give artificial active immunity.
questions.quote: Acquired through the administration of antitoxin, antiserum, convalescent serum, and immunoglobulins

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which is true of attenuated (live, weakened) vaccines compared with inactivated ones?
questions.rationale: Attenuated vaccines usually need a single dose and give long-lasting immunity. Inactivated vaccines need multiple doses and boosters.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Type of Antigen (PDF p. 144)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client on chemotherapy is placed in a room to protect HIM from infection. Which isolation is this?
questions.rationale: Reverse or neutropenic isolation separates an immunocompromised client to prevent him from getting an infection from the environment.
questions.quote: An immunocompromised client is separated to prevent contracting infection from environment.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which statement about transmission-based precautions is correct?
options: They are the second tier of precautions
questions.rationale: Transmission-based precautions are the second tier, added to standard precautions for highly contagious patients. The three types are contact, airborne, and droplet.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A pregnant woman with no history of chickenpox was exposed. Within how many days should VZIG be given?
questions.rationale: Varicella-zoster immune globulin (VZIG) should be given within 10 days of exposure.
explanations: Earlier is fine but not the limit.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Chicken Pox (PDF p. 146)
questions.quote: It should be given within 10 days of exposure

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which statement about chickenpox scabs is correct?
questions.rationale: The main source is respiratory secretions; lesions are of little consequence, and scabs are not infective.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Chicken Pox (PDF p. 145)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Bea, 4, has measles. She has fever, cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis.
questions.stem: During the pre-eruptive stage, the nurse sees a red line on Bea's lower conjunctiva. What is this?
questions.rationale: Stimson's line, a red line on the lower conjunctiva, appears in the pre-eruptive stage of measles along with fever, catarrhal symptoms, and photophobia.
questions.quote: Stimson’s line (red line on the lower conjunctiva)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Bea, 4, has measles. She has fever, cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis.
questions.stem: Bea is sensitive to light. Which nursing care is appropriate?
questions.rationale: Measles causes photophobia, so eye care includes protecting the child from bright light.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Bea, 4, has measles. She has fever, cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis.
questions.stem: Which precautions should the nurse use for Bea?
questions.rationale: Measles is airborne, so standard and airborne precautions are used, ideally in a negative-pressure room.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.situation: Bea, 4, has measles. She has fever, cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis.
questions.stem: Which complication of measles should the nurse watch for MOST in Bea?
questions.rationale: Complications of measles include bronchopneumonia, otitis media, pneumonia, nephritis, and encephalitis.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: For which person is measles vaccine contraindicated?
questions.rationale: Measles vaccine is not given to pregnant women or to people with active TB, leukemia, lymphoma, or depressed immunity.
questions.quote: Measles vaccine should not be given to pregnant women
